findings.title: Second definition of `OptimizedImage.downsize` overwrites the 4/5-argument version
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading by arity. Defining `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` on line 149 completely replaces `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined on line 145. Any caller invoking `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height)` with 4 arguments will now bind `dimensions` to `max_width` and `opts` to `max_height` (causing `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` / `opts[:allow_animation]` to raise `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer`), and any 5-argument call with `opts` will raise `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)`.

findings.title: `tempfile.size` and `tempfile` FD become stale when `OptimizedImage.downsize` replaces the file on disk
findings.body: `Tempfile#size` calls `@tmpfile.stat.size` (`fstat` on the open file descriptor), not `File.size(tempfile.path)`. Inside `OptimizedImage.downsize`, `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!` writes to a temporary file and atomically renames it over `tempfile.path`. Once that rename happens, `tempfile`'s open file descriptor still points to the old, unlinked inode while subsequent `convert` runs modify the new inode at `tempfile.path`. As a result, `tempfile.size` in the `while` condition and in `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)` reports the stale size from the old inode, and reading from the `tempfile` IO object reads the pre-replacement contents. In addition, the loop does not check the boolean return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize`, so unsupported images (such as SVGs, which pass `FileHelper.is_image?`) or failed conversions will pointlessly retry all 5 attempts.

findings.title: Animated GIF downsizing fails when given percentage dimensions like `"80%"`
findings.body: `UploadsController#create_upload` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. For a `.gif` file with `allow_animation` enabled, `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which invokes `gifsicle` with `--resize-fit 80%`. `gifsicle`'s `--resize-fit` option only accepts `WxH` pixel dimensions (scaling by a factor in `gifsicle` requires `--scale`), so `gifsicle` exits with a non-zero status and animated GIFs are never downsized.

findings.title: Hardcoding `maxSizeKB` to 10MB breaks `max_attachment_size_kb` and larger site settings
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` is used for both `'image'` and `'attachment'` uploads, but `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` was replaced with a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. Non-image attachments are not downsized by the server, yet the client will now allow attachments up to 10MB even when `max_attachment_size_kb` is smaller (and will block both attachments and images when `max_attachment_size_kb` or `max_image_size_kb` is configured above 10MB).
